Nonzero-mean zero-shift spatial convergence: rough forcing

Experiment index · Zero-shift functions · m · tau · smooth h · Mean-zero rough study

Problem and relation to the other three notebooks

This fourth added-mean convergence study complements the three restored smooth experiments. It is a new construction from the saved full rough run, rather than an archived nonzero-mean run. All nine exponents \(\alpha=0.9,\ldots,1.7\) and all meshes of the mean-zero rough study are retained. The connected tadpole has stem length 1, loop length 2, and total length 3. We solve \[ u_t+\nu(-\Delta_\Gamma)^{\alpha/2}u=1+g,\qquad u(s,0)=1, \qquad\kappa=0, \] with continuity and Kirchhoff conditions, where \[ g=\sum_{j\ge1}j^{-1}\phi_j,\qquad \phi_j=0\text{ on the stem},\qquad \phi_j(x)=\sin(2^j\pi x)\text{ on the loop }[0,2]. \] The rough part is unchanged: \(g\in L_2\) but has no positive spectral Sobolev regularity. Since every \(\phi_j\) has zero spatial mean, \[ u_{\rm added}(s,t)=u_{\rm rough,zero}(s,t)+1+t, \qquad\bar u(t)=1+t,\qquad M(t)=3(1+t). \] Adding a smooth constant changes neither the forcing’s rough regularity nor the centered fractional diffusion. It does supply mass at rate 3.

Running and knitting

Run setup, parameters, and the computation chunk manually to save results. Knitting only loads that saved file, checks its parameters, and displays results. The computation chunk has eval=FALSE; missing or incompatible results stop knitting without launching a solver.

By default the manual computation reuses the existing full centered rough result after checking all scientific settings. This is sufficient because of the exact invariant-space splitting explained below. To recompute the centered PDE too, set recompute_centered <- TRUE and run the computation chunk. That writes the centered intermediate to a separate filename, leaving the mean-zero study’s saved result unchanged. Worker count affects execution only. Internal checks belong in DOCS/NAP.

knitr::opts_chunk$set(message=FALSE,warning=TRUE,error=FALSE,cache=FALSE,
                      dev="png",fig.width=8,fig.height=5)
if(!requireNamespace("ggplot2",quietly=TRUE)) stop("Install ggplot2 for figures.")

Explicit full-run parameters

The centered settings match true_diff_cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat.Rmd: \(J=5:9\), \(m=14\), \(\tau=8\cdot10^{-7}\), \(K=16\), reference \(J_\star=18\), \(\tau_\star=10^{-5}\), \(\nu=1\), and \(\gamma_*=1/3\). The two added means and the full graph length are explicit.

T_final <- 1
kappa <- 0
gamma_star <- 1/3
alpha_vector <- seq(0.9,1.7,0.1)
diffusion <- 1
J_vector <- 5:9
time_step <- 8e-7
m_fixed <- 14L
reference_cutoff <- 16L
reference_J <- 18L
reference_time_step <- 1e-5
max_tail_squared_fraction <- 0.002
workers <- 9L
initial_mean <- 1
forcing_mean <- 1
graph_length <- 3
recompute_centered <- FALSE
centered_file <- "data_files/true_diff_cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat_paper.rds"
output_file <- "data_files/nonzero_mean_cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat.rds"

# Bundle only the visible parameters above for the shared runner.
settings <- list(study="rough_h",T_final=T_final,kappa=kappa,gamma_star=gamma_star,
    alpha=alpha_vector,diffusion=diffusion,workers=workers,J=J_vector,tau=time_step,m=m_fixed,
    cutoff=reference_cutoff,reference_J=reference_J,reference_tau=reference_time_step,
    max_tail_squared_fraction=max_tail_squared_fraction)
centered_settings <- settings
settings$initial_mean <- initial_mean
settings$forcing_mean <- forcing_mean
settings$graph_length <- graph_length
settings_table <- data.frame(parameter=names(settings),
    value=vapply(settings,function(x) paste(x,collapse=", "),character(1)))

Direct sum of the rough subspace and the constant mode

The centered solver uses the same quarter-loop interval \([0,1/2]\), zero endpoint values, odd reflection, and period-one extension as the mean-zero rough notebook. Four copies reconstruct the full loop; the centered solution is zero on the stem. Its reduced mass matrix is four times the interval mass matrix. On aligned meshes \(h=2^{-J}\) the infinite forcing has the exact FEM load \(\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}j^{-1}(\phi_j,\psi_i)\); these integrals are assembled analytically, without sampling the rough series.

A constant does not belong to that reduced space. The total solution therefore lives in the direct sum of the antisymmetric subspace and the full-graph constant space: \[ U_{\rm added}^k=\mathcal E U_{\rm red}^k+a_k\mathbf1, \qquad a_0=1,\qquad a_{k+1}=a_k+\tau, \qquad a_k=1+t_k. \] Here \(\mathcal E\) is the reflection/extension operator. We evaluate this scalar recurrence by its closed form, so no accumulated time-stepping roundoff is introduced. BRASIL and all shifted sparse solves act only on \(U_{\rm red}^k\), with split_mean=FALSE there. No quarter-interval mean is subtracted. The constant is included on both the stem and loop; the total solution no longer has the centered solution’s odd symmetry.

This is the paper’s zero-shift mean splitting on this invariant subspace: \(\bar U^k=1+t_k\), \(\bar f^k=1\), and \(F_Q^k=F^k-C\mathbf1=F_g\). Consequently the centered evolution is exactly the saved mean-zero rough evolution. Combining it with the separate mean is the numerical scheme itself, without another rational approximation or a new PDE solve. The saved result records the centered result’s file hash, generation date, original source hashes, and parameters separately from this notebook’s generation date and source hashes.

Reference solution and the measured total error

The same reference cutoff is used for the centered continuum solution: \[ u_K(s,t)=\sum_{j=1}^{K}\frac{1-e^{-\nu(\pi2^j)^\alpha t}} {j\nu(\pi2^j)^\alpha}\phi_j(s). \] The added reference is \(u_K+1+t\). Its omitted rough tail has the same bound \[ B_K=\frac{T}{\nu^2\pi^{2\alpha}} \frac{2^{-2\alpha(K+1)}}{(K+1)^2(1-2^{-2\alpha})}. \] We retain the tail check against the centered error, so adding the constant cannot make an inadequate rough reference appear acceptable. Both centered and total tail fractions are reported.

The numerical reconstruction is right-constant in time: on \((t_{k-1},t_k]\) its constant coefficient is \(1+t_k\), while the reference has \(1+t\). The centered error is orthogonal to constants, including under the consistent reference mass matrix by antisymmetry. Thus the actual sampled error is computed exactly by \[ E_{\rm added}^2=E_{\rm centered}^2+ |\Gamma|\sum_\ell w_\ell [\bar f(t_{k(\ell)}-t_\ell^\star)]^2, \qquad |\Gamma|=3,\quad\bar f=1. \] The weights and step indices below match kappa0_sampled_error(): \(w_\ell=t_\ell^\star-t_{\ell-1}^\star\) and \(k(\ell)\) selects the first solver time at or after the reference time. The factor is the full length 3, not the loop length 2 or quarter-loop length 1/2. For an exact time integral and uniform steps the added squared term would be \(T\tau^2\); we instead use the study’s actual sampled quadrature, preserving its norm. The shared constant initial mean cancels from this error.

Raw errors, \(J E_h\), fitted slopes, and \(h^\alpha\) guides are reported as in the mean-zero notebook. The extra temporal term can eventually cause a floor under spatial refinement; it is retained in every total error. mass_by_antisymmetry=0 describes only the centered component. Total initial/final masses and the closed-form mean recurrence are saved separately.

Manual computation

started <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
if(recompute_centered) {
    for(package in c("Matrix","rSPDE","Rcpp","RcppEigen"))
        if(!requireNamespace(package,quietly=TRUE)) stop("Missing package: ",package)
    true_diff <- local({
        extracted <- tempfile("nonzero_mean_rough_",fileext=".R")
        on.exit(unlink(extracted),add=TRUE)
        knitr::purl("kappa0func.Rmd",output=extracted,quiet=TRUE,documentation=0L)
        functions <- new.env(parent=globalenv())
        sys.source(extracted,envir=functions)
        functions
    })
    centered_source <- "data_files/nonzero_mean_rough_centered_intermediate.rds"
    centered <- true_diff$kappa0_compute_study(centered_settings,
        "nonzero_mean_cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat.Rmd",centered_source)
} else {
    centered_source <- centered_file
    if(!file.exists(centered_source)) stop("Missing centered result; set recompute_centered=TRUE and run manually.")
    centered <- readRDS(centered_source)
}
scientific <- setdiff(names(centered_settings),"workers")
bad <- scientific[!vapply(scientific,function(name)
    isTRUE(all.equal(centered$parameters[[name]],centered_settings[[name]],tolerance=1e-12)),logical(1))]
if(length(bad)) stop("Centered result differs for: ",paste(bad,collapse=", "))
stopifnot(is.finite(initial_mean),is.finite(forcing_mean),graph_length==3)
# Identical time-grid and index conventions to the shared sampled solver.
N <- max(1,ceiling(T_final/time_step))
solver_times <- seq(0,T_final,length.out=N+1)
N_reference <- max(1,ceiling(T_final/reference_time_step))
reference_times <- seq(0,T_final,length.out=N_reference+1)
times <- reference_times[-1L]
targets <- findInterval(times,solver_times,left.open=TRUE)
mean_error_squared <- graph_length*sum(diff(reference_times)*
    (forcing_mean*(solver_times[targets+1L]-times))^2)
result <- centered
result$centered_provenance <- list(file=centered_source,
    md5=tools::md5sum(centered_source),generated_at=centered$generated_at,
    source_hashes=centered$source_hashes,parameters=centered$parameters,
    elapsed_seconds=centered$elapsed_seconds)
d <- result$results
d$centered_error <- d$error
d$centered_tail_squared_fraction <- d$tail_squared_fraction
stopifnot(all(d$centered_tail_squared_fraction<=max_tail_squared_fraction))
d$mean_error_squared <- mean_error_squared
d$error <- sqrt(d$centered_error^2+mean_error_squared)
d$corrected_error <- d$J*d$error
d$tail_squared_fraction <- d$cutoff_squared_bound/d$error^2
d$mean_squared_error_fraction <- mean_error_squared/d$error^2
d$initial_mass <- graph_length*initial_mean
d$final_mass <- graph_length*(initial_mean+forcing_mean*T_final)
result$results <- d
result$rates <- do.call(rbind,lapply(alpha_vector,function(a) {
    x <- d[d$alpha==a,]
    data.frame(alpha=a,reference=a,
        raw=unname(coef(lm(log(error)~log(axis),data=x))[2L]),
        observed=unname(coef(lm(log(corrected_error)~log(axis),data=x))[2L]))
}))
result$mean_recurrence <- list(initial=initial_mean,forcing=forcing_mean,
    graph_length=graph_length,steps=N,time_step=T_final/N,
    formula="a_k = initial_mean + forcing_mean * t_k",
    sampled_squared_error=mean_error_squared)
result$parameters <- settings
result$source_hashes <- tools::md5sum(c("kappa0func.Rmd","nonzero_mean_cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat.Rmd"))
result$generated_at <- format(Sys.time(),"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z",tz="Asia/Riyadh")
result$elapsed_seconds <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]-started
result$error_definition <- "sampled full-graph continuum-reference error: centered rough error plus exact constant contribution"
dir.create(dirname(output_file),recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
saveRDS(result,output_file)

Load saved results

scientific <- setdiff(names(settings),"workers")

    isTRUE(all.equal(result$parameters[[name]],settings[[name]],tolerance=1e-12)),logical(1))]
if(length(bad)) stop("Saved result differs for: ",paste(bad,collapse=", "),". Recompute manually.")
cat("Added-mean result generated:",result$generated_at,
    "\nCentered full PDE run generated:",result$centered_provenance$generated_at,
    "\nCentered result:",result$centered_provenance$file,"\n")

Raw and logarithmically corrected spatial convergence

d <- result$results
d$alpha_label <- factor(d$alpha,levels=settings$alpha)
if (settings$study=="m") {
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d,ggplot2::aes(sqrt(m),error,colour=alpha_label,group=alpha_label))+
        ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(shape=resolved))+
        ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+ggplot2::labs(x="sqrt(m)",y="Isolated space-time L2 error",
            colour="alpha",shape="Resolved",title="Zero-shift rational convergence")
} else {
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d,ggplot2::aes(axis,error,colour=alpha_label,group=alpha_label))+
        ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point()+ggplot2::scale_x_log10()+
        ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+ggplot2::labs(x=if(settings$study=="tau") "tau" else "h",
            y="Sampled space-time L2 error",colour="alpha",title="Zero-shift rough convergence: nonzero mean")
}
# Reference curves retain their prescribed slope and are geometrically
# anchored to the data. They are guides, not additional computed errors.
guides <- do.call(rbind,lapply(settings$alpha,function(a) {
    x <- d[d$alpha==a,]
    power <- if(settings$study=="m") -2*pi*sqrt(a/2) else if(settings$study=="tau") 1 else 2
    xx <- if(settings$study=="m") sqrt(x$m) else log(x$axis)
    if(settings$study=="rough_h") power <- a
    x$guide <- exp(mean(log(x$error)-power*xx)+power*xx)
    x
}))
guides$alpha_label <- factor(guides$alpha,levels=settings$alpha)
p <- p+ggplot2::geom_line(data=guides,ggplot2::aes(y=guide),linetype="dashed",alpha=0.6)+
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size=12)+ggplot2::labs(subtitle=sprintf("kappa=0; gamma*=%g",settings$gamma_star))
print(p)

figure_dir <- "data_files/nonzero_mean_cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat"
dir.create(figure_dir,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir,"convergence.pdf"),p,width=8,height=5)

Logarithmically corrected spatial errors

The raw-error plot above includes h-to-the-alpha guides for context; the theoretical logarithmic correction is assessed in this second plot. The corrected slopes are the observed column of the rate table.

corrected_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(d,ggplot2::aes(axis,corrected_error,colour=alpha_label))+
    ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point()+ggplot2::scale_x_log10()+ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+
    ggplot2::labs(x="h",y="J times sampled space-time L2 error",colour="alpha")+
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size=12)
corrected_guides <- do.call(rbind,lapply(settings$alpha,function(a) {
    x <- d[d$alpha==a,]; x$guide <- exp(mean(log(x$corrected_error)-a*log(x$axis)))*x$axis^a; x
}))
corrected_plot <- corrected_plot+ggplot2::geom_line(data=corrected_guides,
    ggplot2::aes(y=guide),linetype="dashed",alpha=0.6)
print(corrected_plot)

ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir,"corrected_convergence.pdf"),corrected_plot,width=8,height=5)
cat("Largest centered squared-tail fraction:",max(d$centered_tail_squared_fraction),"\n")
## Largest centered squared-tail fraction: 1.272736e-05

The .rds file contains the saved settings, errors, rates, source hashes, package versions, and generation timestamp. Figures are redrawn from the saved values when knitting and written to the full-run figure directory. To change the experiment, edit its parameter chunk and run the computation chunk manually before knitting again. Setting NAP.true_diff.recompute or any previous profile option has no effect on knitting these notebooks. Internal tests and smaller exploratory runs belong in DOCS/NAP, not in these report notebooks.
